analysis: Docs-only change to docs/reference/configuration.md: the date bump at line 3 and a rewrite of the 'Cluster runtime facts' section (head lines ~923-1076). The two supplied units are BASE text only (base lines 676-1227). The patch excerpt is truncated, so the head text beyond line 936 and the head-side changes at 958-1008 and 1070-1076 were not visible. The visible patch shows that a signed release may register `cluster_runtime` in its POST /v1/releases payload, and that a coordinator accepting the block derives cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications from it. This is backend, platform-owned behavior. No code, environment-variable defaults, or controls changed in the supplied evidence. Prefix-cache/SSD documentation (T-041) is in the base context only and is not shown as modified. The cluster-approval fetch rules (HTTPS only, no redirect, byte and entry bounds, strict field validation) are unchanged context. A possible threat-model gap: build-derived approvals trust the release-registration channel (A-005, A-011, A-017), which the cluster approval path would now depend on. The coordinator-side implementation is outside the supplied evidence and out of scope, so it is recorded as an unverified contract, not a finding. Further review should confirm that the release-lane documentation (docs/operations/provider-release.md) and the platform implementation keep release-key authorization and qualification independent. Nothing in the visible evidence shows a security regression.
